scope: assembled AI application, provider construction, machine control, and validation topology
objectives: parallel validation lanes with a short critical path
no new top-level runtime island without architecture review
complete AI application capability map with construction and acceptance contracts
mandatory fail-closed architecture acknowledgement for runtime model providers
provider-specific development-agent bootstraps point to one canonical manual
one shared architecture receipt contract across product runtime and repository automation AI providers
machine-readable request lifecycle, data classes, trust zones, environment profiles, envelopes, work packages, and completion criteria
fail-closed data governance and resource admission before external provider I/O
shared ResourceBudget semantics between admission and model routing
one engine-owned provider runtime for text, image, speech, and synchronous compatibility execution
application routes contain no provider credentials or direct vendor SDK imports
one canonical operation identity/state machine across API, orchestration, provider, tool, and stream planes
one transport-neutral resumable event contract with explicit replay and fail-closed backpressure
principles: runtime topology and repository topology are separate contracts linked by this map
canonical roots own behavior; support roots validate, document, automate, or accelerate it
cross-zone calls use declared interfaces instead of ad-hoc environment or path coupling
new long-running services must be declared in both the runtime manifest and this map
structural validation fails closed on unknown nodes, duplicate ownership, cycles, or missing paths
large reconciliation waves integrate by domain and file semantics rather than blind history merge
AI providers are edge adapters; provider SDKs never define application architecture
runtime model providers must load the active construction contract before activation
every capability plane has one owner, explicit dependencies, failure behavior, and acceptance evidence
credential-bearing AI provider surfaces are explicitly inventoried and receipt-gated
provider-neutral libraries may model provider behavior but cannot own undeclared credentials or network activation

AI engine, orchestration, memory, retrieval, resilience, APIs
optional native/JVM acceleration with deterministic fallback
repository structure, integration metadata, machine-facing policy
validation, CI, operator and repository automation
documentation, regression evidence, fixtures and test harnesses

optional Java 21 kernels with Python fallback

cache_boundaries: frontend dependency cache keyed by frontend/yarn.lock
Python dependency cache keyed by packaging/requirements metadata
native/JVM build caches isolated from product shell validation

rules: preserve working runtime entrypoints while moving ownership behind canonical interfaces
prefer adapters and manifests before physical file moves
move files only when import, route, package, and CI ownership are explicit
archive superseded snapshots instead of leaving competing live roots
reconcile large branch families at file/domain level

root_disposition.core: transitional compatibility/control root; converge by import ownership into canonical skeleton domains
root_disposition.eval: evaluation fixtures/support; converge under repository test/evidence ownership
root_disposition.memory: repository session/evidence and backup material; non-runtime, archive generated state
root_disposition.satellites: branch snapshots and recovery material; archive-only, never runtime ownership
root_disposition.deploy.py: legacy root operator entrypoint; converge on python -m skeleton app

invariants: frontend is the only canonical human-interface root
backend and skeleton remain separate API processes until route and dependency ownership converge
browser clients resolve endpoints through frontend/utils/apiBase.ts
runtime service dependencies match skeleton/app/manifest.json
every architecture node and interface reference resolves to a declared node
zone dependency graph is acyclic
runtime dependency graph is acyclic
architecture source files must exist in the repository
architecture changes must preserve a single machine-readable map
runtime model providers cannot activate without a valid architecture/construction receipt
provider-specific development instruction files reference the same canonical construction documents
the AI construction contract enumerates every required capability plane and promotion gate
all credential-bearing AI provider surfaces are declared in the construction contract
runtime and automation provider families share skeleton/provider_contract.py receipt semantics
every open construction gap has exactly one work package and roadmap wave
external provider I/O follows validation -> governance -> admission -> architecture receipt -> client execution
model routing cannot widen ResourceBudget cost, output-token, or wall-time ceilings
runtime-model credentials are owned only by skeleton/provider_runtime.py
undeclared media providers fail closed instead of borrowing another provider credential
operation idempotency identity is distinct from tracing identity
operation terminal states are final
operation stream sequence is monotonic per operation
stream overflow backpressures instead of silently dropping retained events
replay gaps fail closed instead of pretending recovery succeeded
durable operation streams preserve exact-next monotonic sequence transactionally
stream compaction advances an explicit watermark and old cursors fail with replay-gap
durable stream terminal state fences all later writes

construction.policy: contract-before-implementation; undeclared providers, planes, services, roots, and interfaces fail closed

external_interfaces.contract: ProviderRequest -> governance receipt -> admission receipt -> mandatory architecture receipt -> ProviderAdapter -> ProviderResponse
external_interfaces.security: credentials stay inside adapter; data classification and budget are checked before client I/O; HTTPS/custom endpoint policy; bounded timeout/retry

external_interfaces.contract: sanitized repository context -> mandatory automation_model receipt -> bounded model call -> sanitized text
external_interfaces.security: HTTPS-only public endpoint; secrets redacted; bounded response; credentials remain in automation client

external_interfaces.transport: transport-neutral ordered operation event envelope; SSE/WebSocket/polling adapters allowed
external_interfaces.security: operation scoped; bounded JSON payload; no secret-bearing raw logs; replay cursor validated

structural_blueprint.purpose: Bind repository roots, runtime zones, capability planes, physical ownership, state authority, composition roots, and recovery domains into one validator-enforced structural model.

levels.name: repository-root
levels.rule: A top-level live owner must be declared in canonical_roots before it can own runtime behavior.

levels.name: runtime-zone
levels.rule: Zones define legal dependency direction and forbidden ownership.

levels.name: capability-plane
levels.rule: Every construction plane is placed exactly once in one runtime zone.

levels.name: ownership-unit
levels.rule: Each plane has one materialized canonical owner inside its assigned zone.

levels.name: contract-surface
levels.rule: Cross-boundary behavior is explicit, versionable, testable, and receipt-bearing where authority changes.

composition_roots.responsibility: Compose declared runtime services and operator topology; never absorb domain business logic.
Dispatch operator commands into owned engine/application surfaces without creating alternate runtimes.
Mount application routes, middleware, and shared application dependencies; feature logic remains in owned modules.
Mount product providers, guards, and navigation shell; service ownership remains behind canonical API clients.
Construct credential-bearing runtime provider adapters after governance, admission, and architecture receipt checks.
Select among declared provider capabilities using bounded evidence and budgets without performing provider network I/O.

recovery_domains.degraded_mode: fail closed for authority-bearing work; health may remain diagnostic-only
deny or route only to already-declared healthy capacity; never bypass receipts or budgets
bounded stateless mode only where the request contract permits it; never cross tenant boundaries
checkpoint, cancel, or return partial evidence; never silently repeat side effects
health and explicit unavailable responses; resumable operations preserve identity and terminal state
preserve local UI state and surface backend/engine degradation without fabricating completion
fail closed for protected actions and external transfers
freeze promotion and learning mutation while preserving current known-good release

invariants: every construction plane is placed exactly once
plane owner equals the construction contract owner
plane owner is physically contained by its assigned zone
no transitional root owns a construction plane
every declared composition root exists and belongs to its declared zone
every state class has exactly one authority plane and matching owner
every construction plane belongs to exactly one recovery domain
cross-zone plane dependencies follow the zone DAG unless an exact bounded dependency exception is declared
dependency exceptions never widen zone may_depend_on policy and carry a removal condition

dependency_exceptions.rationale: The canonical model-routing policy is still physically owned by backend/core/model_router.py while engine planes consume its provider-neutral routing policy. The zone DAG must not be widened into an engine->application cycle.
dependency_exceptions.removal_condition: Move provider-neutral routing policy into the engine, leave an application compatibility facade, migrate callers, then remove this exception.

dependency_exceptions.rationale: Release orchestration consumes application readiness and release evidence; it does not grant the engine ownership of application runtime behavior.
dependency_exceptions.removal_condition: Replace the construction prerequisite with an explicit release-evidence interface when the release evidence contract is promoted.

dependency_exceptions.rationale: Release orchestration consumes product build/E2E evidence; it does not import or own product-shell behavior.
dependency_exceptions.removal_condition: Replace the construction prerequisite with an explicit product release-evidence interface when the release evidence contract is promoted.
